objective.statement: Fix the Home View bordered div so its border is dashed, keeping the existing green colour (owner feedback: dashed border only, keep the green colour).

complexity.rationale: One Tailwind class added to one element in HomeView.tsx plus one new component test; no new state, dependency or contract.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The bordered div on the Home View keeps its green border colour (border-green-500); the colour is not changed to blue.
The bordered div renders a dashed border style (border-dashed).
The div carries neither border-blue-500 nor border-red-500, and its other behaviour (200px size, centred 8px text, 2px width, rounded corners, text) is unchanged.
HomeView.tsx carries a one-line comment next to the bordered div explaining why its border is dashed. The comment is source-only and changes no rendered output.

in.statement: src/views/home/HomeView.tsx: add border-dashed to the bordered div's classes and keep border-green-500 unchanged.
src/views/home/HomeView.component.test.tsx: add one dashed-border test; keep the existing green-border test as the colour regression guard.
src/views/home/HomeView.tsx: add one single-line comment explaining the dashed border, placed directly above the bordered div.

out.statement: Changing the border colour to blue or any other colour; renaming the redBorderedSquare test id, the aria-label "Red bordered square", or the test titles that mention red; any other element's border; theme tokens; new dependencies or config.

observations.statement: Render HomeView: the div with data-id home-view-red-bordered-square has className border-2 border-green-500 and no border-dashed, so it shows a solid green border.

The green colour was introduced deliberately by the earlier change-home-view-border-to-green workflow and is now explicitly kept by the owner. HomeView.component.test.tsx 'should render a green border instead of a red one' stays valid and stays unchanged.
"Dashed" means the border-dashed utility with the existing 2px width. Raw palette classes are already used on this element rather than theme tokens.
The 'green bordered div' is the single bordered div in HomeView; the legacy red-bordered naming of its test id and aria-label is left alone to keep the fix minimal.

Revision 2 supersedes the rejected revision 1 plan, which also changed the colour to blue (border-blue-500, p-assume-blue). The owner rejected that: the colour stays green and only the dashed style is added. p-assume-blue is kept in provenance as history only.

The comment is exactly one line (a single JSX comment, written in the style of the surrounding code), stating that the border is dashed on purpose. Owner feedback 3 shortened the revision 3 comment from up to two lines to one. It is verified by review, not by a test, because a comment has no runtime behaviour.

provenance.source: Card: Bug Fix - Wrong border colour. The green bordered div should be blue and dashed.
Card says blue without a shade; conservative choice is Tailwind blue-500, matching the green-500 it replaces.
Card does not ask to rename the red-bordered test id or aria-label; conservative choice is to leave them untouched.
Existing behaviour of the div (size, centring, text size, text) must stay as covered by existing tests.

Feedback says dashed without a width; conservative choice is the border-dashed utility with the existing border-2 width.
Owner rejected the revision 2 plan (gate record a5588506a5d6e6eea02de1f716cc79917a5d690d1d7032390ed924508908de1d). Feedback (quoted data): "Also add a short comment explaining the dashed border".
Feedback does not say what the comment should say or where; conservative choice is one short comment directly above the bordered div.
Owner rejected the revision 3 plan (gate record 8e51d060a6d70a79a40e1d8c82df00a9a1d88168c7c517300513fd432dff4696). Feedback (quoted data): "keep the comment but shorten it to one line".

approvals.requirement: The owner must approve this plan before any test or production file is written.

decisions.rationale: Awaiting owner approval of the plan.

capabilityOwners.rationale: The border is static render output on HomeView; no state is involved.
Border styling is not client state.

unit.rationale: No logic or pure function changes; the fix is a className change.

component.rationale: The rendered HomeView element must carry the dashed class while keeping the green one.

integration.rationale: No cross-module behaviour changes; the full npm test suite still runs as regression verification (App.component.test.tsx renders HomeView).

e2e.rationale: Pure styling of an already component-tested element; no routed flow changes.

increments.behavior: The Home View bordered div renders border-dashed, keeps border-green-500, and a one-line comment explains the dashed border.
increments.doneWhen: The dashed component test passes, the existing green-border test still passes unchanged, the explanatory comment is present, the full suite is green, and tsc and eslint are clean.

tests.description: HomeView bordered div has class border-dashed.

expectedRedEvidence.expectedFailure: expect(className).toContain('border-dashed') fails because the div has no dashed utility.

verification.requirement: HomeView dashed test passes and the other HomeView tests, including the green-border test, still pass.
Full suite (npm run test), tsc build and eslint pass with no regression in App tests.
Review of the diff confirms a one-line comment (exactly one line) explaining the dashed border sits directly above the bordered div in HomeView.tsx and nothing else in the rendered output changed.
